chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal and Muhammad ibn Isa, all from Al-Reza (peace be upon him), and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Zareef, from his father Zareef ibn Nasih, from Abdullah ibn Ayoub, from Abu Amr al-Mutatabbib, who said:

I presented to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) what Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) had issued verdicts regarding the blood money (diyat). Among what he issued verdicts on, he issued a verdict regarding the body and made it six obligations: the self, the sight, the hearing, the speech, the deficiency of the voice from croaking and hoarseness, and the paralysis of the two hands and the two legs.

Then he made for each of these a compurgation (qasamah) according to the amount the blood money reached. He made for the self in case of deliberate killing fifty men, and for the self in case of accidental killing twenty-five men. And for whatever of the injuries reached a blood money of one thousand dinars, he made six persons. And whatever was less than that, it is by calculation from six persons.

And the compurgation is for the self, the hearing, the sight, the intellect, the voice from croaking and hoarseness, and the deficiency of the two hands and the two legs; so it is from the six parts of the man.
ai.seo_question: What are the categories of bodily injury and the corresponding blood money compurgation numbers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Al-Reza (AS) clarifies the application of qasamah (compurgation) in diyat cases, establishing that the number of swearers scales with the severity of the injury, ranging from five to fifty men. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that bodily impairments are treated as fractional parts of the soul, thereby linking physical compensation directly to the spiritual value of the individual. This ruling underscores the precision of Imami fiqh in balancing legal evidence with the proportional justice of blood money.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, and Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus,
(It has been narrated) both together from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>,
and and number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Zareyf, from his father Zareyf Bin Naih, from Abdullah Bin Ayoun, from Abu Amro Al Mutatayyab who said,

‘I presented to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> the verdict of Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> regarding the wergild. So from what he<sup>asws</sup> had issued verdict with regarding the body, and made it six obligations of the self, and the sight, and the hearing, and the speech, and deficiency of the voice from the croaking, and the paralysis of the two hands, and the two legs.

And he<sup>asws</sup> made to be regarding the self upon the erroneous (killing), being twenty-five men (swearing), and upon what his wergild reached from the injuries sustained, a thousand Dinars, being six persons (swearing). So whatever was less than that, it would be by that counting, from six persons (swearing).

And the compurgation (sworn endorsements) regarding the self, and the hearing and the sight, and the intellect, and the voice, from the croacking, and the deficiency of the two hands and the two legs, so it is from six parts of the man’.
